A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AudioLBM and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I. The appendices are retained in v3, following an added NeurIPS checklist; their relocation does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original super-resolution experiments, component ablations, reconstruction evaluations, and a listening study with 20 participants, including results in Tables 1–14 and Figure 1.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and the listening study described in Appendix G.4.

M1.justification: The waveform VAE, latent bridge objectives and sampler, frequency conditioning, cascaded stages, and waveform/latent augmentation procedures are unchanged. Corrections from 'argumentation' to 'augmentation' do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training datasets in Table 15 and evaluate VCTK, ESC-50, SDS, internal 48/96/192 kHz datasets, and generated-audio listening scenarios. No dataset, domain, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the benchmark, compression, efficiency, modeling-space, and qualitative comparisons. The newly cited FreeAudio work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and the appendices retain the same sample sizes, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and sampling procedures. Appendix G.4 also retains the same listening-test design; the checklist does not document a revised protocol.

E4.justification: The frequency-awareness, compression/KL, augmentation, post-processing, filtering, and modeling-space analyses are retained, as are the qualitative case studies. Correcting Figure 10's panel references adds no new analysis or evidence.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty estimates, error bars, or significance procedures are added or revised. Checklist item 7 newly answers 'No' about statistical-significance reporting, but the actual reporting practice remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains zero-shot VCTK LSD 0.753, and Table 3 retains cascaded LSD 1.216 and 1.365 for the 96 kHz and 192 kHz evaluations, respectively.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, bandwidth estimator, and bridge-model derivation are unchanged, including Equations (1)–(18) and Appendix C. No proof, formal assumption, or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: waveform-latent bridge modeling, frequency-aware any-to-any training, and cascaded super-resolution up to 192 kHz. The novelty and performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning informative priors, compression tradeoffs, cascading artifacts, data scarcity, inference cost, and potential misuse remain unchanged. The checklist mostly supplies generic assurances or references existing discussion rather than adding substantive scientific qualifications.

D1.justification: The new checklist explicitly states that code is unavailable at this stage and asserts that training data were selected under permissive licenses. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs establish neither a new release nor changed implementation, hyperparameters, or study procedures.

R1.justification: v3 adds FreeAudio as reference 39 to the existing long-duration inference discussion. The broader research positioning is unchanged; the QA-MDT and Bridge-SR reference edits update bibliographic information rather than introduce different works.

P1.justification: v3 inserts a standardized NeurIPS checklist while preserving the scientific narrative and appendix organization. Local edits correct augmentation terminology, clarify the Table 4 reference in Appendix B.1.1, update bibliographic details, and add Zehua Chen as a corresponding author.

P2.justification: Figure 10's caption and accompanying references change the filtering panels from (c)–(f) to (c)–(e), and output panels from (g)–(i) to (f)–(h), matching the existing figure. Figures and table structures are otherwise retained, with limited author-block and text-layout changes.

improvement.justification: Terminology and cross-reference corrections improve clarity, particularly around Table 4 and Figure 10. However, the added checklist introduces reporting inconsistencies: item 14 marks human-subject research not applicable despite Appendix G.4's retained 20-participant study, while item 15 answers yes about approval-related disclosure without supplying that information. With the scientific evidence unchanged, these limited clarity gains and new reporting defects leave the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
